title: Kernel fingerprint registry and staged profile rollout for hybrid MHA/GQA/MoE
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When onboarding hybrid attention models (MHA/GQA/MoE variants) we lack a canonical, queryable registry that ties a model artifact version to an exact kernel fingerprint, ABI tag, and the performance profile used in production. That gap causes: flaky rollouts when a compiled kernel regresses for a specific sequence length distribution; manual, error-prone pinning; and slow rollback when customers hit tail-latency or memory regressions.

Goal: Implement a kernel fingerprint registry and an automated staged publish/rollout flow that: (1) computes a deterministic fingerprint for compiled kernel bundles (including ABI/flags/arch target), (2) stores per-model-version performance profiles (latency percentiles, throughput, memory), (3) exposes an API used by the onboarding pipeline to pin a model->kernel binding, and (4) supports blue/green staged profile rollouts with SLO gating and automated rollback triggers.

Constraints: Must be compatible with existing profile storage formats, not require full recompilation for every minor commit, and support fast lookups in the routing layer (microsecond-latency). Rollout decisions should be observable and reversible by the Console.

Success metrics: reduce manual pin-related incidents by 80% on first deploy, detect perf regressions within 15 minutes of rollout, and enable safe canaries for 95% of new model versions.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel registry service that accepts a compiled bundle and returns a stable fingerprint and ABI tags.
Per-model-version profile objects published to the registry with latency p50/p95/p99, throughput traces, and memory envelopes.
Onboarding pipeline can pin model versions to registry fingerprints via an idempotent API call.
Console shows staged rollout status (canary %, health, perf deltas) and allows manual promote/rollback.
Automated SLO gate that aborts rollout and triggers rollback when p99 increases > 30% or latency SLA breached for 5m window.
End-to-end e2e test harness exercising a synthetic MoE/MHA/GQA model demonstrating canary detection and rollback.
Docs and runbook entries for operations and oncall to handle edge cases.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design fingerprint schema and registry API (fingerprint fields: kernel-hash, ABI-tag, arch, compile-flags, toolchain-version, optional perf-hash).
Phase 2: Prototype local fingerprint extractor in onboarding runner; produce sample fingerprint for the sample-moe-1 model and persist to registry.
Phase 3: Extend existing profile publisher to attach runtime telemetry snapshots (sequence-length histograms, KV cache hit rates).
Phase 4: Build staged rollout controller (canary percent, evaluation window, SLO rules) and integrate with routing config service for atomic swaps.
Phase 5: Instrument Console endpoints and add visualizations for fingerprint diffs and perf deltas.
Phase 6: Run controlled rollout on internal QA tenants, gather metric baselines, iterate on gate thresholds.
Phase 7: Document API and update onboarding checklist to include 'publish fingerprint' and 'run canary harness'.
telemetry_queries: SELECT model_version, registry_fingerprint, percentile(50, latency_ms) as p50, percentile(95, latency_ms) as p95, percentile(99, latency_ms) as p99 FROM inference.tokens WHERE registry_fingerprint IS NOT NULL AND timeframe = '5m' GROUP BY model_version, registry_fingerprint;
select count(*) as regressions from perf_alerts where alert_type = 'fingerprint_perf_regression' and created_at >= now() - interval '7 days';
SELECT registry_fingerprint, avg(kv_cache_hit) as kv_hit FROM inference.traces WHERE model_version = 'sample-moe-1' GROUP BY registry_fingerprint;
comments: 2026-03-01 Aisha Patel: Kickoff - scoped initial MVP to registry API + local extractor. Noted need for deterministic compile flags extraction; assigned Liam for prototype.

2026-03-03 Liam Chen: Prototype PR opened - fingerprint extractor emits kernel-hash + toolchain tag. Local bench shows identical bundles across two build machines when toolchain-version matches. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4921

2026-03-05 Carlos Gomez (infra): Reviewed PR - requested include 'sequence-length-signature' in profile metadata to catch distribution-sensitive kernels. Also recommended adding 'compatibility_labels' for fallback kernels.
2026-03-07 Maya Rios (PM): Confirmed SLO gating thresholds for canaries: p99 delta > 30% OR p95 delta > 50ms for >5m window should fail canary. Asked to make thresholds configurable per-tenant.

2026-03-09 Liam Chen: Bench update - sample-moe-1 canary detected a memory leak in compiled kernel when ABI-tag = 'nvcc-11.8-fast-mem', triggered automatic rollback in staging. Reproduced, filed follow-up ENG-813580 to fix compilation flag handling.
2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Design review scheduled with SRE and Console for 2026-03-12. Next steps: implement registry persistence with TTL for ephemeral builds and add query index for routing lookup.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only on staging cluster with 1% canary for 30m, SLO gate evaluation every 5m.
Beta: internal tenants, 5% canary for 1h with automated rollback webhook enabled.
GA: 50% gradual ramp across Dedicated pools, then full promote once 24h stable windows pass. Manual override available in Console.
Rollback: immediate switch to previous fingerprint via routing atomic swap; notify oncall and create regression ticket automatically.
risks: Fingerprint collisions if hash scheme not robust - mitigate by including compile metadata and toolchain version.
Storing sensitive compile flags - ensure registry stores only sanitized flag sets and respects KMS policies.
Large registry growth for frequent internal builds - use TTL and dedupe by perf-hash heuristics.
False positives in SLO gate from noisy telemetry - require min sample counts before evaluation.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint stability across identical build inputs.
Integration tests: onboarding pipeline publishes fingerprint and Router resolves to correct kernel bundle.
Canary e2e: synthetic traffic with variable sequence lengths to validate gate thresholds and KV cache warmup behavior.
Chaos scenario: simulate partial compilers failures and ensure fallback to generic kernel label works and doesn't block traffic.
